question: What is the main goal of food budgeting in clinical nutrition?

options.A: To plan food spending without compromising nutritional health
options.B: To buy only the cheapest food available on the market
options.C: To eliminate all spending on processed and convenience foods
options.D: To calculate the exact daily calorie intake of a patient

explanation: Spot on! Food budgeting is all about balancing your pocket with your plate so you never have to sacrifice good health just to save some cash. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h1)

question: Why do families on a tight budget often experience a drop in their diet quality?

options.A: Local markets stop selling fresh vegetables to low-income earners
options.B: Wholesale food vendors refuse to sell small quantities to families
options.C: Nutritional requirements naturally decrease when a person has less money
options.D: They replace nutrient-dense foods with cheap, highly processed options

explanation: Exactly. When funds run low, it's easy to lean towards cheaper, filling items that lack the vital nutrients our bodies really need. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h1)

question: What does the term 'nutrient density' mean?

options.A: Providing many vitamins and minerals relative to the calorie count
options.B: Being imported from foreign countries to ensure high quality
options.C: Containing only fats and proteins with zero carbohydrates
options.D: Having high amounts of calories and sugar in a small serving

explanation: Spot on! Nutrient-dense foods pack a heavy punch of vitamins and minerals into every single calorie, giving you the best value for your health. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h2)

question: A client on a strict budget needs affordable protein. Which of these is the best recommendation?
explanation: You got it! Beans and local eggs are cheap, easy to find, and give fantastic protein without burning a hole in your pocket. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h2)

question: What is the main advantage of creating a weekly meal plan?

options.A: It stops impulsive buying and reduces food expenses
options.B: It ensures all family members eat the exact same food portions
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever visit a local open-air market
options.D: It guarantees that weight loss will occur within seven days

explanation: That's right! Having a clear plan stops those random, hunger-driven shopping trips that cost way more than expected. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h3)

question: Why does batch cooking help save money?

options.A: It guarantees that food will never spoil under any condition
options.B: It requires buying expensive kitchen appliances upfront
options.C: It forces family members to eat less food overall
options.D: It reduces energy consumption and limits ingredient waste

explanation: Spot on! Cooking larger pots at once uses less cooking gas or kerosene and ensures ingredients get used up before going bad. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h3)

question: Why is it a bad idea to go grocery shopping on an empty stomach?

options.A: It makes non-essential snacks and food items look more tempting
options.B: It slows down the speed at which cashiers process payments
options.C: It causes sudden low blood pressure in the store aisle
options.D: It prevents the buyer from finding the correct grocery store

explanation: So true! Shopping while hungry always makes everything look delicious, leading to costly impulse buys you didn't budget for. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h4)

question: What is the benefit of comparing unit prices while shopping?

options.A: It determines how long the food item will last in the refrigerator
options.B: It helps the cashier calculate the total sales tax accurately
options.C: It reveals the true cost of an item per standard weight or volume
options.D: It shows which brand contains the highest amount of artificial preservatives

explanation: Brilliant! Unit pricing cuts through sneaky package sizes to show you which product actually gives you more value for your money. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h4)

question: What is the difference between a 'use-by' date and a 'best-before' date?

options.A: Use-by is for canned goods, while best-before is for fresh meat
options.B: Use-by relates to safety, while best-before relates to quality
options.C: Use-by is set by the government, while best-before is optional
options.D: Use-by means the food is free, while best-before means it is costly

explanation: Spot on! 'Use-by' is about food safety (don't risk food poisoning), while 'best-before' is just about peak flavor and crunch. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h5)

question: A family has leftover cooked rice and vegetables. What is the best way to handle them?

options.A: Throw them in the bin immediately to avoid food poisoning
options.B: Refrigerate them promptly and transform them into a fried rice dish
options.C: Feed them exclusively to house pets instead of humans
options.D: Leave them on the kitchen counter overnight for breakfast

explanation: Exactly! Cooling leftovers quickly and repurposing them prevents waste and turns yesterday's food into a brand-new meal. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h5)

question: Why are open-air markets often cheaper for food shopping in Nigeria than large supermarkets?

options.A: They do not require any form of monetary currency exchange
options.B: They only sell imported items that have expired
options.C: They avoid high markups for packaging and retail overhead costs
options.D: They receive government subsidies that lower all food prices

explanation: You nailed it! Open-air markets bring produce straight from farms without all the expensive branding, packaging, and high shop rents. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h6)

question: Which Nigerian food item is an excellent local source of both plant protein and healthy fats?
explanation: Spot on! Egusi is packed with valuable plant proteins and healthy fats, making it a powerhouse for local nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h6)

question: What is the most important approach when counseling a client on a tight food budget?

options.A: Scolding them for wasting money on fast food
options.B: Providing a rigid meal plan that cannot be changed
options.C: Insisting they buy only organic imported foods

explanation: Exactly! Listening without judgment builds trust and helps you truly understand your client's financial reality. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h7)

question: Why should a nurse involve the client in modifying their own meal plan?

options.A: It eliminates all future health risks related to poor nutrition
options.B: It relieves the nurse from doing any paperwork during the visit
options.C: It ensures the client feels ownership and will stick to the changes
options.D: It proves that the client has a better education than the nurse

explanation: Spot on! When clients help build their own plan, they feel a sense of ownership and are much more likely to stick with it. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h7)
